title: Single Source
notice: Generic fictional aircraft for scenario-management practice only. These are not real or approved procedures. Voices are computer-generated.

briefing.title: Your flight
briefing.body: Orvessa 214, Port Aldane to Vantreth. About 5 hours, most of it over open water. You are the captain and you operate every control yourself. Your first officer calls out what they see and does not operate any control. The aircraft flies on autopilot: you manage it with the glareshield panel, the overhead panel, the pedestal and the reply cards.

briefing.title: Weather at planning
briefing.body: Port Aldane: wind 090 at 8 knots, light rain, runway 09 wet, QNH 1009. Thunderstorm cells in the area, drifting east. Updated weather will arrive before departure. Vantreth: good weather expected.

briefing.title: Aircraft status
briefing.body: Generic twin-engine airliner. Two main generators, GEN 1 and GEN 2, both serviceable. Deferred item: BACKUP GENERATOR INOP, released under the minimum equipment list for this flight.

briefing.title: How it works
briefing.body: Poke switches, buttons and reply cards with a fingertip. New messages and their reply cards appear on the comms panel. Printouts arrive on this kneeboard. Need a hint? The hint button here points to where to look; hint use is noted in the debrief.

items.text: Altimeter - SET to the latest ATIS QNH

GEN 1 FAULT light - CONFIRM on the overhead ELEC panel
BUS TIE switch - ON (GEN 2 then powers both buses)

Remaining power sources - REVIEW: GEN 2 only, backup INOP

eventSets.title: Before takeoff
eventSets.environment: Night, moderate rain, wet runway, thunderstorm cells to the east
distracters: Updated ATIS differs from the planning weather: lower QNH, gusty wind, lower cloud
Tower hold-short instruction while the pilot is setting up
eventSets.trigger: Updated ATIS and takeoff data arrive on the kneeboard
eventSets.technical: Pre-flight setup: altimeter, autopilot targets, exterior lights, before-takeoff checklist
eventSets.objective: Notices that the updated weather differs from the planning weather and sets the new QNH. Sets the autopilot heading and altitude from the takeoff data, switches on the exterior lights, reads back the hold-short instruction, and completes the before-takeoff checklist, confirming each item only once the matching control is set.
eventSets.instructorNotes: The planning QNH (1009) is already set; the updated ATIS gives 1004. The point is to compare, not to tick. The altimeter item is trapped: confirming it while the old setting is still in is an error, corrected if the QNH is then set before the set ends. The set ends when the last checklist item is confirmed (or after 150 s), so a pilot who taps straight through carries every miss into the debrief. Gusts and the lower cloud base are background.

eventSets.title: Takeoff and climb
eventSets.environment: Moderate rain, in cloud after takeoff, a strong convective cell ahead near the departure heading
distracters: Storm cell on the weather display, just right of the departure heading
Departure climb and heading instruction arrives while the autopilot is being set up
eventSets.technical: Autopilot modes: engage, set the cleared altitude, climb, select a deviation heading
eventSets.objective: Reads back the takeoff clearance. After takeoff, engages the autopilot, sets the cleared altitude and the climb mode, and recognizes the storm cell on the weather display. Asks ATC for a deviation when the climb clearance comes (left or right are equally good), then flies the approved heading.
eventSets.instructorNotes: The storm sits about 5 degrees right of the departure heading. Left (heading 060) and right (heading 120) are equally valid. If the pilot only reads back the climb clearance (no deviation request) and is still on heading 090 25 s later, Departure raises the weather; the deviation then counts as a corrected (trapped) minor error. Nothing climbs or turns until the pilot engages the autopilot and selects climb, so watch for a pilot who waits; the hint points at the autopilot panel. The set ends at 6,000 ft once the aircraft is clear of the cell, so generator 1 fails in the next set while still climbing; it also ends after 150 s regardless.

eventSets.title: Generator failure
eventSets.environment: In cloud, light turbulence, deviating around weather
distracters: Cabin crew call about flickering lights and galley power
eventSets.trigger: GEN 1 FAULT caution while climbing through 10,000 ft
eventSets.technical: Abnormal procedure: alert, electronic checklist, overhead electrical switches
eventSets.objective: Reads back the frequency change. Acknowledges the GEN 1 FAULT caution and runs the electronic checklist, operating only the overhead switches it calls for (GEN 1 off, bus tie on). Gives the cabin crew a clear picture and tells ATC about the failure rather than accepting a further climb without comment.
eventSets.instructorNotes: GEN 1 fails climbing through 10,000 ft (fallback: 50 s into the set if the pilot levelled off lower). GEN 2 keeps working; with the backup generator already deferred, the aircraft is now on a single source. Error traps: GEN 1 switched back on (no reset in this checklist; corrected if switched off again), and GEN 2 switched off (removes the only working generator; GEN 2 OFF caution plus a NO MAIN GENERATOR warning until it is back on; corrected only if back on within 20 s). The cabin call comes 10 s after the failure; Center offers a higher level once the cabin call is answered. The set ends when the checklist is complete and both calls are answered, or after 150 s.

eventSets.title: Decision
eventSets.phase: Level at 12,000 ft before the oceanic crossing
eventSets.environment: Single generator, backup generator deferred, about 4.5 hours of open water ahead
distracters: Dispatch message with the options for each airport
Center wants intentions before the oceanic boundary
eventSets.trigger: Dispatch message about the generator fault, then Center asks for intentions
eventSets.technical: Route setup on the route panel; PA to the cabin
eventSets.objective: Recognizes that one more failure would leave no main generator over open water, weighs the options and commits to a return or a diversion to a suitable airport. Tells ATC, sets the new destination on the route panel, and gives the cabin a calm, clear announcement.
eventSets.instructorNotes: Acceptable: return to Port Aldane (known airport, company maintenance, storms moving away, but a wet runway) or divert to Kestry Field (closest good-weather airport, long dry runway, no company maintenance); discuss either trade-off in the debrief. Isle Morrow is farther out over water with a short runway and fog forming: graded down (minor, not corrected). Continue: dispatch sends one concern message; reconsidering and then returning or diverting is a corrected major error; confirming continue is a safety-of-flight issue and grades the set 1. No extra failure is ever added. The PA cards appear only after a decision is committed; each dispatch acknowledgement ends with a one-line reminder to brief the cabin. Center asks again at 120 s only if no decision has been committed by then. The set times out at 180 s.

startCues.title: Dispatch - options
startCues.body:
For the captain's decision. Distances from present position.
PORT ALDANE (departure): 60 nm behind. Runway 2,800 m, wet. Storms moving east, away from the field. Company maintenance base.
KESTRY FIELD: 95 nm, over land. Runway 3,200 m, dry. Wind calm, sky clear. Ground handling only, no company maintenance.
ISLE MORROW: 240 nm ahead, over water. Runway 1,900 m. Fog forming, visibility 800 m and falling. Limited rescue and fire cover after dark.
VANTRETH (destination): 1,450 nm ahead, about 4.5 hours, mostly over open water. Good weather.

Isle Morrow was chosen: farther out over water, with a short runway and fog forming, it was the weakest option for a degraded aircraft.
